Filter features by m/z, retention time, mass defect, or target list

mc_filter_peak.Rd

Apply selected feature-property bounds or match a list of m/z and retention-time targets. Store values and filtering decisions for plotting.

mc_filter_peak(x, filters = NULL, parameters = mc_peak_parameters(), 
    targets = NULL, target_text = NULL)

Arguments

x

A metabocensor_result returned by mc_prepare() or a filtering function.

filters

Any of "mz", "rt", "rmd", "amd", and "target". NULL uses parameters$peak_filters; the default selects no filters.

parameters

Named list from mc_peak_parameters(), specifying enabled bounds and target-matching tolerances.

targets

Target data frame or local CSV filename with m/z and retention time in minutes. Use columns named mz and rt; if recognizable names are absent, the first two columns are used.

target_text

Optional comma-separated target rows as one string, with or without a header. These rows are combined with targets and duplicate m/z-RT pairs are removed.

Details

All selected filters must pass. Minimum and maximum bounds are inclusive and enabled independently. Nonfinite property values fail an active bound.

Nominal mass is floor(mz + 0.5). Relative mass defect (RMD) is 1e6 * (mz - nominal_mass) / mz, in ppm; absolute mass defect (AMD) is abs(mz - nominal_mass), in Da. These calculations use the observed m/z, not a reconstructed neutral mass.

Target matching requires both m/z and RT to fall within their tolerances. target_peak_action = "remove" removes matches; "keep" retains only matches. Nonfinite target rows are discarded. An empty usable target list does not filter features; a nonempty keep-only list with no matches raises an error.

Each filtering stage can be used once per result object. To change its settings, start again from the object saved before that stage. Separate stages may be called in any order; each receives only the features retained so far.

Value

The updated result with retained table, removed_ids$peak, and updated counts. peak stores the settings and target_matches records accepted target-feature matches and mass/RT differences.

peak_tbl includes all input features with Feature, mz, RT, RMD, AMD, per-filter pass_* columns, target_hit, and final keep.

See also

mc_peak_parameters, mc_plot_peak, mc_run

Examples

peak_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "orbi_iimn_gnps_quant.csv",
  package = "MetaboCensoR", mustWork = TRUE
)
imported <- mc_prepare(
  peak_file, type = "mzmine",
  sample_keywords = c(".mzML", "Peak area")
)
# Illustration of peak filtering, not the published Orbi settings.
peak_options <- mc_peak_parameters(
  mz_min_enable = TRUE, peak_mz_min = 200,
  rt_min_enable = TRUE, peak_rt_min = 1
)
after_peak <- mc_filter_peak(
  imported, filters = c("mz", "rt"), parameters = peak_options
)
head(after_peak$peak_tbl)
#>   Feature       mz        RT       RMD       AMD pass_mz pass_rt pass_rmd
#> 1     108 148.0277 0.3691534  187.4459 0.0277472   FALSE   FALSE     TRUE
#> 2     181 169.0462 0.3699988  273.5672 0.0462455   FALSE   FALSE     TRUE
#> 3     175 128.0198 0.3707691  154.4012 0.0197664   FALSE   FALSE     TRUE
#> 4     231 216.9513 0.3714030 -224.6412 0.0487362    TRUE   FALSE     TRUE
#> 5      43 234.9614 0.3725722 -164.4909 0.0386490    TRUE   FALSE     TRUE
#> 6     145 244.9475 0.3726993 -214.2316 0.0524755    TRUE   FALSE     TRUE
#>   pass_amd target_hit pass_target  keep
#> 1     TRUE      FALSE        TRUE FALSE
#> 2     TRUE      FALSE        TRUE FALSE
#> 3     TRUE      FALSE        TRUE FALSE
#> 4     TRUE      FALSE        TRUE FALSE
#> 5     TRUE      FALSE        TRUE FALSE
#> 6     TRUE      FALSE        TRUE FALSE
mc_plot_peak(after_peak, interactive = FALSE)
